questions.q: The hydrocarbon $(X)$ with molar mass $80 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $90 \%$ carbon has $\ldots\ldots$ degree of unsaturation.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: $\therefore$ Empirical formula is $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_4$ Molecular mass $=80 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. questions.q: \(9.3 \mathrm{~g}\) of pure aniline is treated with bromine water at room temperature to give a white precipitate of the product ' \(\mathrm{P}\) '. The mass of product ' \(\mathrm{P}\) ' obtaind is \(26.4 \mathrm{~g}\). The percentage yield is _______ \(\%\).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: $93 \mathrm{~g}$ of aniline produces $330 \mathrm{~g}$ of $2,4,6-$ tribromoaniline. Hence $9.3 \mathrm{~g}$ of aniline should produce $33 \mathrm{~g}$ of 2, 4, 6-tribromoaniline. Hence percentage yield $\frac{26.4 \times 100}{33}=80 \%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
CH4+   2O2⟶   CO2+2H2O

10016    20832

Number of molesstoichiometric coefficient for CH4=6.251  Number of molesstoichiometric coefficient for O2=6.52=3.25

The reagent with lower ratio of number of moles to stoichiometric coefficient is called limiting reagent.

Hence, O2 is limiting reagent

Limiting reagent decides the amount of product,

As per the equation 2 moles of O2 gives rise to 1 mole of CO2, So 6.5 moles of O2 gives 6.52 moles of CO2

⇒nCO2=6.52

So mass of CO2=6.52×44=143gm

questions.q: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of gaseous hydrocarbon on combustion gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of water vapour. Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is _______.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction can be represented as 

CxHy+x+y4O2→xCO2+yH2O

At STP, 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L

10 mL of hydrocarbon, 50 mL of water and 40 mL of carbon dioxide corresponds to 0.45, 2.23,  and 1.79 moles respectively.

Hence, the combustion of 1 mole of hydrocarbon will produce 5 moles of water and 4 moles of carbon dioxide.

Thus, the molecular formula contains 4 carbon atoms and 10 hydrogen atoms.

The hydrocarbon is C4H10 and the combustion reaction is 

C4H10+6.5O2→4CO2+5H2O

x+y=4+10=14

Hence the Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is 14.
